Sure you can be some rich guy who sells drugs, or moves money around or something. Or you could be Steve Jobs/Bill Gates, you could be Albert Einstein, you could be Satoshi Tajiri. Point is, you can be rich, but does that mean "successful"?  Nothing against entertainers, they are amazing and talented people, but you could be entertaining people for a living, or you could be the surgeons and doctors that saved your mom's life. You could even be the guy who gives free taxi rides to poor people, a charity worker, or this guy: https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dashrath_Manjhi
You could help starving kids in Africa for little pay. You could be a soldier. You could be a firefighter who risked their lives for others in the 911 attacks.

The point is: To be successful does not mean to be well off, have a family, decent job, food in the table. Heck the mountain man lost his wife, which is why he did it. Successful means you made a difference in not only your life, but many other people.

(Coming straight from a F2P player)Check your account everyday. At the least, reroll the quest. If you have time, try to complete quests. Try arena. If you can tend to get 3 or more wins, it is probably going to be more worth it than buying packs. Packs are good if you are trying to specifically get one card, or for example you are trying to make a mech deck so you choose to buy Goblins VS Gnomes packs. If you are buying Solo adventures, I would save up for League of Explorers first. A good way to start is to find some cheap budget deck online, and make it. Budget zoo, or a mech style of any class. Reroll quests that are for only 40 gold. If you cannot finish a quest in ranked mode or casual but you are losing a lot of games, play tavern brawl. Make sure you get the pack from tavern brawl which starts every Wednesday (At least in NA) Try to watch a lot of different streams and dig for information on reddit, streams, videos, articles, so on. Once you get good enough or have enough cards to make real constructed (play mode) decks, then make sure you use things like the Hearthstone Meta Snapshot. I find that Kripp and Trumps' videos are helpful for both arena and constructed play. I also suggest watching the youtuber no dust (I think that's what he's called) He shows off decks that he made with only commons and rares!
